descriptionChirho: The basic Qal stem expressing the intransitive emotion of rejoicing or being glad; covers all finite verb forms (perfect, imperfect, imperative, jussive, cohortative, consecutive, waw-conjunctive) across all persons, numbers, and genders, with consistent cross-linguistic reflexes: Arabic fariha/yafraḥu, Korean gippŏhada, Swahili -furahi, Hindi ānandita honā.
The Qal infinitive construct with prepositions (le- 'to rejoice', ke- 'when/as rejoicing'), used as a verbal complement or temporal clause; Arabic ʿinda faraḥi, Swahili kufurahi.

The adjective śāmēaḥ used substantively with the article to denote persons who are in a state of rejoicing or gladness ('the rejoicing ones'); Arabic al-fariḥūna, Korean gippŏhanŭn jadŭl, Swahili wanaofurahi.

The Piel (intensive-causative) stem meaning to cause someone to rejoice, to gladden or make joyful; covers all Piel finite forms (perfect, imperfect, imperative, consecutive), infinitive absolute, and participles with consistent causative reflexes: Arabic farraḥa (Form II), Korean gippeuge hada, Swahili -furahisha (causative), Hindi ānandita karnā.
The Hifil (causative) stem meaning to cause someone to rejoice; semantically close to Piel but a distinct verb stem; Arabic ʾafraḥta (Form IV), Korean gippeuge hasyŏssnida, Swahili -furahisha.
